g.text: DIODE SMALL-SIGNAL AC & ZENER VOLTAGE REGULATOR ARCHITECTURE
Dynamic AC Resistance, Zener vs Avalanche Physics, Shunt Regulator Engine & Precise R_s Sizing Bounds
GATE 2027 TITAN SUITE
FIGURE 2 • 4K VECTOR
1. Small-Signal AC Principle & Dynamic Resistance (r_d)
• Principle of Small Signal: Superimpose a tiny time-varying AC signal v_d(t) onto DC operating point (V_DQ, I_DQ).
Total Voltage: v_D(t) = V_DQ + v_d(t) Total Current: i_D(t) = I_DQ + i_d(t)
• Dynamic (AC) Resistance Derivation:
r_d = dV_D / dI_D |_(Q) = η · V_T / I_DQ ≈ 26 mV / I_DQ (for η = 1 at 300 K)
• DC Static Resistance vs AC Dynamic Resistance:
R_DC = V_DQ / I_DQ vs r_d = η V_T / I_DQ ⇒ r_d << R_DC in forward bias!
• Small-Signal AC Equivalent Circuit:
- DC independent voltage sources → Short circuit (0 V).
- DC independent current sources → Open circuit (0 A).
- Coupling and bypass capacitors (large C) → Short circuit for AC: X_C = 1/(ω C) ≈ 0.
- Diode replaced strictly by dynamic incremental resistance r_d.
★ Small-Signal Validity Criterion: v_d << η V_T ≈ 5 mV (peak-to-peak must not cause distortion).
★ Attenuator Application: Diode r_d controlled via DC current I_DQ creates variable gain AC attenuator.
2. Zener Diode Physics & Breakdown Mechanisms
• Definition: Heavily doped PN junction engineered to operate safely in the reverse breakdown region.
Comparison of Breakdown Regimes:
PARAMETER
ZENER BREAKDOWN
AVALANCHE BREAKDOWN
Doping Level
Heavily Doped (1 in 10³)
Lightly Doped (1 in 10⁸)
Breakdown Voltage
V_Z < 6 V (Typically 2V - 6V)
V_Z > 6 V (Typically > 8V)
Physical Mechanism
Quantum Tunneling / Field Emission
Impact Ionization / Carrier Multiplication
Depletion Width (W)
Ultra-Narrow (< 10 nm)
Relatively Wide
Temp Coefficient (TC)
NEGATIVE (V_Z decreases as T rises)
POSITIVE (V_Z increases as T rises)
• Zero-TC Reference: At V_Z ≈ 5.6 V, Zener & Avalanche mechanisms balance out, giving near ZERO temperature coefficient!
Zener Operating States in Circuit Analysis:
1. Forward Bias: Acts as a normal forward-biased diode with V_D = 0.7 V.
2. Reverse Bias below breakdown (0 < V_R < V_Z): Acts as open-circuit (I_Z ≈ 0).
3. Reverse Breakdown (V_R ≥ V_Z): Clamps voltage at V_Z (Ideal battery V_Z or V_Z + I_Z · r_z).
★ Vital Condition: For regulation, Zener current MUST satisfy: I_Z,min ≤ I_Z ≤ I_Z,max (where I_Z,max = P_Z,max / V_Z).
3. Zener Shunt Voltage Regulator Design & Boundary Analysis Engine
Zener Shunt Regulator Topology

R_L

V_o = V_Z
I_s
I_Z

KCL: I_s = I_Z + I_L where I_s = (V_in - V_Z) / R_s
Open-Circuit Thevenin Test for Zener Breakdown
1. Temporarily REMOVE the Zener diode from the circuit and calculate open-circuit voltage V_Th across its terminals:
V_Th = V_in · [ R_L / (R_s + R_L) ]
2. Decision Diagnostic:
✓ If V_Th ≥ V_Z: ZENER IS IN BREAKDOWN! Output is regulated: V_o = V_Z. Proceed with normal regulation equations.
✗ If V_Th < V_Z: ZENER IS OFF (I_Z = 0)! Regulator FAILS! Output drops to unregulated value: V_o = V_Th < V_Z.
★ Critical Condition for Breakdown: R_L ≥ (R_s · V_Z) / (V_in - V_Z) (Establishes absolute minimum R_L,min)
CASE 1: LINE REGULATION (Variable V_in, Constant R_L)
• Condition: Input voltage fluctuates: V_in,min ≤ V_in ≤ V_in,max. Load resistance R_L is fixed.
Constant Load Current: I_L = V_Z / R_L = constant.
A. Minimum Input Voltage (V_in,min) Condition:
To maintain breakdown, Zener current must not drop below minimum knee current I_Z,min (typically 1 mA - 5 mA):
I_s,min = I_Z,min + I_L ⇒ V_in,min = V_Z + (I_Z,min + I_L) · R_s
B. Maximum Input Voltage (V_in,max) Condition:
Zener current must not exceed maximum thermal limit I_Z,max = P_Z,max / V_Z to prevent destruction:
I_s,max = I_Z,max + I_L ⇒ V_in,max = V_Z + (I_Z,max + I_L) · R_s
★ Safe Input Voltage Window: V_in,min ≤ V_in ≤ V_in,max
CASE 2: LOAD REGULATION (Constant V_in, Variable R_L)
• Condition: Input voltage V_in is fixed. Load varies: R_L,min ≤ R_L ≤ R_L,max (or 0 ≤ I_L ≤ I_L,max).
Constant Total Source Current: I_s = (V_in - V_Z) / R_s = constant = I_Z + I_L.
A. Minimum Load Resistance (R_L,min) / Maximum Load Current (I_L,max):
Occurs when load draws maximum current, starving Zener to minimum knee current I_Z,min:
I_L,max = I_s - I_Z,min ⇒ R_L,min = V_Z / I_L,max = V_Z / (I_s - I_Z,min)
B. Maximum Load Resistance (R_L,max) / Minimum Load Current (I_L,min):
Occurs when load is detached (no load, R_L = ∞, I_L = 0) or draws minimum current; Zener absorbs peak current:
I_Z,peak = I_s - I_L,min ≤ I_Z,max (If R_L = ∞, must ensure I_s ≤ I_Z,max)
★ Open-Circuit Load Trap: If load is disconnected, ALL source current flows through Zener: I_Z = I_s!
CASE 3: COMBINED REGULATION — SIZING OF SERIES RESISTOR (R_s)
When BOTH input voltage varies (V_in,min to V_in,max) AND load varies (I_L,min to I_L,max), R_s must satisfy dual inequalities:
UPPER BOUND: Maximum Allowable R_s (R_s,max)
Evaluated at WORST-CASE STARVATION: Lowest input voltage V_in,min AND Highest load current I_L,max:
R_s,max = (V_in,min - V_Z) / (I_Z,min + I_L,max)
If R_s > R_s,max, Zener falls out of breakdown and regulation fails at low supply.
LOWER BOUND: Minimum Allowable R_s (R_s,min)
Evaluated at WORST-CASE OVERHEATING: Highest input voltage V_in,max AND Lowest load current I_L,min:
R_s,min = (V_in,max - V_Z) / (I_Z,max + I_L,min)
If R_s < R_s,min, Zener current exceeds I_Z,max and burns out thermally at high supply.
★ GOLDEN DESIGN WINDOW: R_s,min ≤ R_s ≤ R_s,max
If calculations yield R_s,min > R_s,max, NO single passive resistor can regulate the circuit across specified input/load extremes;
either a higher power-rated Zener diode (larger I_Z,max) or active feedback regulation must be employed.
